scene.title: Implementing Debounce in TypeScript
scene.subtitle: Optimizing function execution frequency

answer.headline: A debounce function delays execution until a set period of inactivity passes, preventing excessive function calls.
body: Debouncing is a performance pattern used to ensure that time-consuming tasks do not fire too often. When you wrap a function in a debounce, it does not execute immediately when called. Instead, it starts a timer. If the function is called again before the timer expires, the previous timer is cancelled and a new one starts. Only when the timer finally completes does the original function execute.

This is critical for browser events that can fire hundreds of times per second, such as window resizing, scrolling, or user input in a search box. By implementing debounce, you conserve system resources and prevent redundant network requests or expensive DOM recalculations, ensuring a smoother user experience.
caveats: The returned function maintains internal timer state, which persists across calls.
Debouncing can introduce a slight perceived lag since the function waits for a delay.

modules.headline: Common scenarios for debouncing

items.label: Reduced server load
items.detail: Prevents redundant API calls by aggregating rapid requests into one.

items.label: Improved UI responsiveness
items.detail: Prevents main-thread blocking by limiting heavy recalculations.

items.label: Input latency
items.detail: Users may perceive a slight delay as the application waits for the debounce window.

spotlight.label: Use debounce when you only care about the final state of a sequence of rapid events rather than every intermediate state.
